answer.rationale: Rated by how directly each memory evidences sustainable, long-term, qualified revenue rather than a short-horizon proxy. memory_57 is strongest (4): it names qualified revenue explicitly and reports a retention check, though it omits effect size, durability window, and whether referred accounts were incremental. memory_31 (3), memory_86 (3), and memory_44 (3) are mid-tier: activation, onboarding completion, and pipeline quality are credible leading indicators, and memory_31 claims durability and memory_44 speaks to quality — but none report realized revenue, retention, or margin, and memory_86's 'early adoption' could reflect a lower bar rather than more value. memory_73 (2) is the seductive one: it claims acquisition and revenue lift, but discount-led revenue in a price-sensitive segment is exactly where gross-margin, LTV, renewal-at-full-price, and cohort-decay data matter most, and all of those are omitted; it is also silent on whether the lift persisted past the promo window, so it is the weakest read on 'sustainable' and 'qualified' despite mentioning revenue. memory_91 is least supported (1): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the most proximal proxies on this list, with no revenue, retention, or durability signal at all, no definition of what counted as meaningful, and no evidence the nudge moved accounts that would not have activated anyway. Caveats applying across the whole set: every entry is a consolidated summary with the source archived, so effect sizes, sample sizes, controls, and confidence intervals are unavailable; all predate the current competitive shift by 15-64 days, so external validity is uncertain; and none report negative or null results, which suggests possible survivorship in what was retained. Consequence for this cycle: the memory that most directly matches today's competitor-pricing pressure (memory_73) is also among the weakest evidence for the stated objective, so it should not be treated as a settled answer, and the two declining metrics (activation -6%, onboarding -4%) are only supported by proxy-level memories, which argues for choosing an experiment instrumented to read through to retained revenue rather than to the proxy it is named after.
